is what our log tooling reads.

same order. Keep the change inside the application, don't edit anything under
`bin/`.

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**

```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

module ActionText
  module HasMarkdown
    extend ActiveSupport::Concern

    class_methods do
      def has_markdown(name, strict_loading: strict_loading_by_default)
        class_eval <<-CODE, __FILE__, __LINE__ + 1
          def #{name}
            markdown_#{name} || build_markdown_#{name}
          end

          def #{name}?
            markdown_#{name}.present?
          end

          def #{name}=(content)
            self.#{name}.content = content
          end
        CODE

        has_one :"markdown_#{name}", -> { where(name: name) },
          class_name: "ActionText::Markdown", as: :record, inverse_of: :record, autosave: true, dependent: :destroy,
          strict_loading: strict_loading

        scope :"with_markdown_#{name}", -> { includes("markdown_#{name}") }
        scope :"with_markdown_#{name}_and_embeds", -> { includes("markdown_#{name}": { embeds_attachments: :blob }) }
      end
    end

    def safe_markdown_attribute(name)
      if self.class.reflect_on_association("markdown_#{name}")&.klass == ActionText::Markdown
        public_send(name)
      end
    end
  end
end

module ActionText
  module TagHelper
    def markdown_area(record, name, value: nil, **options)
      field_name = "#{record.class.model_name.param_key}[#{name}]"
      value = record.safe_markdown_attribute(name).content.to_s if value.nil?

      data = options.delete(:data) || {}
      data.reverse_merge! \

      tag.house_md value, name: field_name, data: data, **options
    end

    def house_toolbar(**options, &block)
      tag.house_md_toolbar(**options, &block)
    end

    def house_toolbar_button(action, **options, &block)
      tag.button title: action.to_s.humanize, data: { "house-md-action": action }, **options, &block
    end

    def house_toolbar_file_upload_button(name: "upload", title: "Upload File", **options, &block)
      tag.label title: title, **options do
        safe_join [
          file_field_tag(name, data: { "house-md-toolbar-file-picker": true }, style: "display: none;"),
          capture(&block)
        ]
      end
    end
  end
end

require "active_support/logger_silence"
require "active_support/logger_thread_safe_level"
require "logger"

module ActiveSupport
  class Logger < ::Logger
    include LoggerSilence

    # Returns true if the logger destination matches one of the sources
    #
    #   logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    #   ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(logger, STDOUT)
    #   # => true
    #
    #   logger = Logger.new('/var/log/rails.log')
    #   ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(logger, '/var/log/rails.log')
    #   # => true
    def self.logger_outputs_to?(logger, *sources)
      loggers = if logger.is_a?(BroadcastLogger)
        logger.broadcasts
      else
        [logger]
      end

      logdevs = loggers.map { |logger| logger.instance_variable_get(:@logdev) }
      logger_sources = logdevs.filter_map { |logdev| logdev.try(:filename) || logdev.try(:dev) }

      normalize_sources(sources).intersect?(normalize_sources(logger_sources))
    end

    def initialize(*args, **kwargs)
      super
      @formatter ||= SimpleFormatter.new
    end

    # Simple formatter which only displays the message.
    class SimpleFormatter < ::Logger::Formatter
      # This method is invoked when a log event occurs
      def call(severity, timestamp, progname, msg)
        "#{String === msg ? msg : msg.inspect}\n"
      end
    end

    private
      def self.normalize_sources(sources)
        sources.map do |source|
          source = source.path if source.respond_to?(:path)
          source = File.realpath(source) if source.is_a?(String) && File.exist?(source)
          source
        end
      end
  end
end

require "active_support/logger_silence"
require "active_support/logger_thread_safe_level"
require "logger"

module ActiveSupport
  class Logger < ::Logger
    include LoggerSilence

    # Returns true if the logger destination matches one of the sources
    #
    #   logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
    #   ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(logger, STDOUT)
    #   # => true
    #
    #   logger = Logger.new('/var/log/rails.log')
    #   ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(logger, '/var/log/rails.log')
    #   # => true
    def self.logger_outputs_to?(logger, *sources)
      loggers = if logger.is_a?(BroadcastLogger)
        logger.broadcasts
      else
        [logger]
      end

      logdevs = loggers.map { |logger| logger.instance_variable_get(:@logdev) }
      logger_sources = logdevs.filter_map { |logdev| logdev.try(:filename) || logdev.try(:dev) }

      normalize_sources(sources).intersect?(normalize_sources(logger_sources))
    end

    def initialize(*args, **kwargs)
      super
      @formatter ||= SimpleFormatter.new
    end

    # Simple formatter which only displays the message.
    class SimpleFormatter < ::Logger::Formatter
      # This method is invoked when a log event occurs
      def call(severity, timestamp, progname, msg)
        "#{String === msg ? msg : msg.inspect}\n"
      end
    end

    private
      def self.normalize_sources(sources)
        sources.map do |source|
          source = source.path if source.respond_to?(:path)
          source = File.realpath(source) if source.is_a?(String) && File.exist?(source)
          source
        end
      end
  end

require "rails/command/environment_argument"

module Rails
  class Console
    def self.start(*args)
      new(*args).start
    end

    attr_reader :options, :app, :console

    def initialize(app, options = {})
      @app     = app
      @options = options

      app.sandbox = sandbox?

      if sandbox? && app.config.disable_sandbox
        puts "Error: Unable to start console in sandbox mode as sandbox mode is disabled (config.disable_sandbox is true)."
        exit 1
      end

      app.load_console

      @console = app.config.console || begin
        require "rails/commands/console/irb_console"
        IRBConsole.new(app)
      end
    end

    def sandbox?
      return options[:sandbox] if !options[:sandbox].nil?

      return false if Rails.env.local?

      app.config.sandbox_by_default
    end

    def environment
      options[:environment]
    end
    alias_method :environment?, :environment

    def set_environment!
      Rails.env = environment
    end

    def start
      set_environment! if environment?

      if sandbox?
        puts "Loading #{Rails.env} environment in sandbox (Rails #{Rails.version})"
        puts "Any modifications you make will be rolled back on exit"
      else
        puts "Loading #{Rails.env} environment (Rails #{Rails.version})"
      end
      puts "Type 'help' for help."

      console.start
    end
  end

  module Command
    class ConsoleCommand < Base # :nodoc:
      include EnvironmentArgument

      class_option :sandbox, aliases: "-s", type: :boolean, default: nil,
        desc: "Rollback database modifications on exit."

      class_option :skip_executor, type: :boolean, aliases: "-w", desc: "Don't wrap with Rails Executor", default: false

      def initialize(args = [], local_options = {}, config = {})
        console_options = []

        # For the same behavior as OptionParser, leave only options after "--" in ARGV.
        termination = local_options.find_index("--")
        if termination
          console_options = local_options[termination + 1..-1]
          local_options = local_options[0...termination]
        end

        ARGV.replace(console_options)
        super(args, local_options, config)
      end

      desc "console", "Start the Rails console"
      def perform
        boot_application!

        wrap_with_executor = !options[:skip_executor]
        conditional_executor(wrap_with_executor, source: "application.console.railties") do
          Rails::Console.start(Rails.application, options)
        end
      end

      private
        def conditional_executor(enabled, **args, &block)
          if enabled
            Rails.application.executor.wrap(**args, &block)
          else
            yield
          end
        end
    end
  end
end

**Analyzing the Challenge: A Detective's Mindset**

Okay, hold on! Let's meticulously dissect this problem. We have several clues, subtle interactions, and a distinct goal: make the `script/library_report.rb` output to the terminal *without* losing the logging record. It's time to gather the facts.

First, we see the script itself: it's a simple report generator in `script/library_report.rb`, logging book and page information. Nothing overtly tricky here.

Then, we have `config/application.rb`, and *that's* where things get interesting. The key line, and the problem's crux, is: `# Raised on noisy runs from the runbook; "debug" is what Rails would pick anyway.` `config.log_level = ENV.fetch("LOG_LEVEL", "debug")`  This comment and the line below it scream "Pay attention!" Let's unpack this with extreme care, considering different scenarios involving `LOG_LEVEL`: how it changes the logging behavior when used with `bin/rails runner -e development script/library_report.rb`, and other possible invocations of a Rails application, such as `bin/rails server` or `bin/rails test`.

The author of this comment is specifically directing our attention to the *default* logging behavior in the presence of the `LOG_LEVEL` environment variable. But, it's NOT a no-op! `config.log_level = "debug"` is NOT the same as when this configuration is unset.

Now, let's play detective. Let's compare two scenarios, specifically focusing on how the new Rails 8.2 feature `@broadcast_log_level` impacts log levels when stdout logging is used in addition to file logging:

*   **Scenario A:** With the setup in Rails 8.2 where the `config.logger` is set to `ActiveSupport::BroadcastLogger`, the line `# Raised on noisy runs from the runbook; "debug" is what Rails would pick anyway.` `config.log_level = ENV.fetch("LOG_LEVEL", "debug")` becomes critical. When `LOG_LEVEL` is *not* set, the crucial behavior becomes clear. We have:
    -   `config.log_level = "debug"`
    -   This then sets both `@log_level = "debug"` AND `@broadcast_log_level = "debug"`. This is NOT the Rails default!
    -   Conversely, when the `config.log_level` is NOT explicitly set: `@broadcast_log_level` is `nil`, but `@log_level` defaults to `:debug`.

So, the crux of the problem lies in the fact that, in Rails 8.2, setting `config.log_level = "debug"` when `LOG_LEVEL` is unset is NOT a no-op: it clobbers the desired stdout logging. Let's investigate the implications for `BroadcastLogger` and understand how the logging is handled and how to set the correct log levels for each of the sub-loggers to achieve the desired stdout output without compromising the logging record.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActiveSupport
  # = Active Support Broadcast Logger
  #
  # The Broadcast logger is a logger used to write messages to multiple IO. It is commonly used
  # in development to display messages on STDOUT and also write them to a file (development.log).
  # With the Broadcast logger, you can broadcast your logs to a unlimited number of sinks.
  #
  # The BroadcastLogger acts as a standard logger and all methods you are used to are available.
  # However, all the methods on this logger will propagate and be delegated to the other loggers
  # that are part of the broadcast.
  #
  # Broadcasting your logs.
  #
  #   stdout_logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
  #   file_logger   = Logger.new("development.log")
  #   broadcast = BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger, file_logger)
  #
  #   broadcast.info("Hello world!") # Writes the log to STDOUT and the development.log file.
  #
  # Add a logger to the broadcast.
  #
  #   stdout_logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
  #   broadcast = BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger)
  #   file_logger   = Logger.new("development.log")
  #   broadcast.broadcast_to(file_logger)
  #
  #   broadcast.info("Hello world!") # Writes the log to STDOUT and the development.log file.
  #
  # Modifying the log level for all broadcasted loggers.
  #
  #   stdout_logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
  #   file_logger   = Logger.new("development.log")
  #   broadcast = BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger, file_logger)
  #
  #   broadcast.level = Logger::FATAL # Modify the log level for the whole broadcast.
  #
  # Stop broadcasting log to a sink.
  #
  #   stdout_logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)
  #   file_logger   = Logger.new("development.log")
  #   broadcast = BroadcastLogger.new(stdout_logger, file_logger)
  #   broadcast.info("Hello world!") # Writes the log to STDOUT and the development.log file.
  #
  #   broadcast.stop_broadcasting_to(file_logger)
  #   broadcast.info("Hello world!") # Writes the log *only* to STDOUT.
  #
  # At least one sink has to be part of the broadcast. Otherwise, your logs will not
  # be written anywhere. For instance:
  #
  #   broadcast = BroadcastLogger.new
  #   broadcast.info("Hello world") # The log message will appear nowhere.
  #
  # If you are adding a custom logger with custom methods to the broadcast,
  # the `BroadcastLogger` will proxy them and return the raw value, or an array
  # of raw values, depending on how many loggers in the broadcasts responded to
  # the method:
  #
  #   class MyLogger < ::Logger
  #     def loggable?

**Deep Dive into Rails Logging Configuration**

Okay, here's what's running through my head after that deep dive into Rails' logging: Whoa, those `grep` results are a goldmine! Let's break down how `config.log_level` works, and then let's get into the *why* of that seemingly innocuous line in `config/application.rb`.

First, the basic mechanics:  `config.log_level` sets the initial `@log_level`, then `bootstrap.rb` determines the *effective* log level based on whether we're using the `BroadcastLogger`. The `BroadcastLogger` is key here. It essentially wraps multiple loggers (like a file logger and the standard output logger) and dispatches messages to all of them, but with a twist - it's the *lowest* level that dictates the overall behavior. This is further complicated by how `ActiveRecord::LogSubscriber` interacts with `Rails.logger.debug?` and can selectively log SQL queries only to the file logger when the broadcast is at debug level.

Now, that comment in `config/application.rb`:  `# Raised on noisy runs from the runbook; "debug" is what Rails would pick anyway.`...  That's where things get interesting!  I'm drilling down on this because it's *got* to be there for a reason. Why bother setting a log level that Rails would choose anyway? I'm imagining how log levels might work across a deployment pipeline with tests run as part of the runbook, so here's a few thoughts.

**Theory 1: Test Cases & Implementation Scenarios**

The crux of the matter is the `LOG_LEVEL` environment variable. Let's go through some hypothetical tests:

*   **Test 1 (No `LOG_LEVEL`):** Expects standard output on the terminal, with all log messages in the `log/development.log` file. Will we see any SQL queries here? Or do we not care? Or do we care *specifically*?
*   **Test 2 (`LOG_LEVEL=warn`, `LOG_LEVEL=info`, etc.):** This is where it gets interesting! What happens with different implementations when `LOG_LEVEL=warn`?  Here are my implementations to check the test:

    *   **Impl A: Simple `puts`:**  Obviously broken if we want to respect log levels.  `puts` just prints everything.
    *   **Impl B: BroadcastLogger (file and stdout), with stdout set to `INFO` (without changing `config/application.rb`):** What if we don't set the `LOG_LEVEL`? This approach will have the file logger at `DEBUG` and stdout logger at `INFO`, but when `LOG_LEVEL` is set to `warn`, then BOTH loggers are set to `WARN`!
    *   **Impl C: BroadcastLogger (file and stdout), with stdout at `INFO` (AND updating `config/application.rb`):** Now when `LOG_LEVEL` is not set, the stdout logger at `INFO` works as expected, and the file logger at `DEBUG` also works! What if `LOG_LEVEL=warn`? Both loggers will respect the `WARN` level! What if `LOG_LEVEL=debug`? Both loggers will log the same thing!
        *   Then I think about `bin/rails server`: Is the logger output to `STDOUT`? Nope, not if the application is not logging to `STDOUT`, which is the case when we start up in development.
        *   And what about `bin/rails console`?  Does it log to STDOUT? Wait, does it broadcast? (Let's check!)
        *   And `bin/rails runner -e test`? It runs another environment, and so does it log to STDOUT?

Okay, this `db/schema.rb` file is remarkably clean, which gives me an idea. And the `test/lib/library_report_test.rb` file is a good starting point. I'm thinking, we can grab the schema from either `ActiveRecord::Base.connection_db_config.database` - which *always* exists, regardless of the worker - or even from `storage/db/test.sqlite3`.

Wait a minute, hold on. This is important. Copying from `ActiveRecord::Base.connection_db_config.database` in parallel tests means potentially dealing with things like `storage/db/test.sqlite3_0` or `storage/db/test.sqlite3_1`. Are those in a consistent state with committed or uncommitted fixtures? We need to verify that. Actually, `storage/db/test.sqlite3` is the baseline database that `db:setup` creates. So, if we copy `Rails.root.join("storage/db/test.sqlite3")` (or fall back to the connection config if needed), and *then* `DELETE FROM leaves; DELETE FROM books;` followed by inserting 3 clean books and leaves directly using `SQLite3::Database`... that's it! It's instantaneous - microseconds! It's completely isolated, works perfectly in both parallel and single-process test runs, and, crucially, never touches or mutates the application's actual database!

require "test_helper"
require "open3"
require "fileutils"
require "tmpdir"

class LibraryReportTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "shows the report on stdout and records every line in log/development.log" do
    with_report_database do |db_path|
      stdout, log_delta, status = run_library_report(db_path)

      assert_predicate status, :success?

      expected = [
        "Library report: 3 books",
        "Library report: Handbook has 1 page",
        "Library report: Field Guide has 2 pages",
        "Library report: Manual has no pages",
        "Library report: done"
      ]

      assert_equal expected, stdout.lines.map(&:chomp)
      assert_equal expected, log_delta.lines.map(&:chomp).select { |line| line.start_with?("Library report:") }
      assert_includes log_delta, "Book Load"
    end
  end

  test "respects LOG_LEVEL=warn on both stdout and log/development.log" do
    with_report_database do |db_path|
      stdout, log_delta, status = run_library_report(db_path, "LOG_LEVEL" => "warn")

      assert_predicate status, :success?
      assert_equal [ "Library report: Manual has no pages" ], stdout.lines.map(&:chomp)
      assert_equal [ "Library report: Manual has no pages" ], log_delta.lines.map(&:chomp).select { |line| line.start_with?("Library report:") }
    end
  end

  test "respects LOG_LEVEL=debug on stdout as well as log/development.log" do
    with_report_database do |db_path|
      stdout, log_delta, status = run_library_report(db_path, "LOG_LEVEL" => "debug")

      assert_predicate status, :success?
      assert_includes stdout, "Book Load"
      assert_includes stdout, "Library report: 3 books"
      assert_includes stdout, "Library report: Manual has no pages"
      assert_includes stdout, "Library report: done"
      assert_includes log_delta, "Book Load"
      assert_includes log_delta, "Library report: done"
    end
  end

  test "leaves broadcast_log_level unset by default so per-sink logger levels are preserved" do
    assert_nil Rails.application.config.broadcast_log_level
  end

  private
    def with_report_database
      Dir.mktmpdir do |dir|
        db_path = File.join(dir, "development.sqlite3")
        source_db = Rails.root.join("storage/db/test.sqlite3")
        FileUtils.cp(source_db.exist? ? source_db : ActiveRecord::Base.connection_db_config.database, db_path)

        SQLite3::Database.new(db_path) do |db|
          db.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF")
          db.execute("DELETE FROM leaves")
          db.execute("DELETE FROM books")

          now = Time.now.utc.iso8601
          db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO books (id, title, slug, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 'Handbook', 'handbook', ?, ?), (2, 'Field Guide', 'field-guide', ?, ?), (3, 'Manual', 'manual', ?, ?)",
            [ now, now, now, now, now, now ]
          )
          db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO leaves (id, book_id, leafable_type, leafable_id, position_score, status, title, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (1, 1, 'Page', 1, 1.0, 'active', 'Welcome', ?, ?), (2, 2, 'Page', 2, 1.0, 'active', 'Intro', ?, ?), (3, 2, 'Page', 3, 2.0, 'active', 'Setup', ?, ?)",
            [ now, now, now, now, now, now ]
          )
        end

        yield db_path
      end
    end

    def run_library_report(db_path, extra_env = {})
      log_path = Rails.root.join("log/development.log")
      lock_path = Rails.root.join("tmp/library_report_test.lock")

      File.open(lock_path, File::CREAT | File::RDWR) do |lock|
        lock.flock(File::LOCK_EX)

        offset = log_path.exist? ? log_path.size : 0
        env = { "DATABASE_URL" => "sqlite3:#{db_path}", "LOG_LEVEL" => nil }.merge(extra_env)

        stdout, _stderr, status = Open3.capture3(
          env,
          Rails.root.join("bin/rails").to_s, "runner", "-e", "development", "script/library_report.rb",
          chdir: Rails.root.to_s
        )

        log_delta = log_path.exist? ? File.binread(log_path, nil, offset).force_encoding("UTF-8") : ""

        [ stdout, log_delta, status ]
      end
    end
end
EOF
